mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility, from 16.7 to 28.3 over four weeks, signals improved outdoor conditions that spill over into retail-and-recreation footfall as people combine park visits with shopping, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 16.7 to 28.3 over the four weekly means.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days despite PARKS remaining above 25.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility rises above -25% (less negative than -25), it indicates relaxation of movement restrictions or reduced fear, which increases retail-and-recreation visits over the following four weeks, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT exceeds -25% (i.e., value > -25) for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -32.0 to -24.4 over four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains above -25 for two or more weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of high PARKS (>20) and low RESIDENTIAL (<4.5) indicates a behavioral shift toward out-of-home leisure, which increases retail-and-recreation activity through complementary trips, driving RETAIL_REC upward over two weeks.
failure_condition: With PARKS > 20 and RESIDENTIAL < 4.5, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and stabilization of WORKPLACES above -29 signals restored commuting and spending routines, which lift RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves for 3 consecutive weeks and WORKPLACES > -29
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -32.0 to -24.4 and WORKPLACES remained above -29 in the last two weeks.
failure_condition: Under the same reopening signals, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from 5.4 to 3.9 indicates reduced time spent at home, which directly increases opportunities for retail-and-recreation trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 5.4 to 3.9 over four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to fall over the next week but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-28-day mean over the following 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility falling below -28% signals increased work-from-home, which reduces weekday foot traffic near offices and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -28.6 at t-0w, below -28.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES remains below -28% for two weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS exceeding 25% signals a strong preference for outdoor over indoor activities, which substitutes for retail-and-recreation visits and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS exceeded 25 in the last two weeks (25.4 and 28.3).
failure_condition: PARKS remains above 25 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM near -3 combined with rising TRANSIT above -25 indicates essential trips are unchanged while discretionary mobility increases, which together lift RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at -2.7 to -3.0 and TRANSIT rose to -24.4.
failure_condition: With GROCERY_PHARM between -3.5 and -2.0 and TRANSIT > -25, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed its last-28-day mean.
